interest: This document provides valuable insight into diplomatic coordination and immigration policies between Imperial Japan and Nazi Germany in late 1938, specifically in the immediate aftermath of Kristallnacht. It highlights efforts to restrict the influx of German Jewish refugees through a bilateral understanding requiring prior Japanese approval before Germany would issue passports valid for travel to Japan. Although the file here consists solely of the List of Papers docket sheet, it directs historians to key cross-referenced records (894.111/75) concerning early Japanese refugee policy and Axis administrative cooperation.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.5562, File 572) consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet concerning immigration to Japan from Germany. It indexes one entry, a communication (No. 383) dated November 29, 1938, from Charles R. Cameron in Tokyo, which is cross-referenced to decimal file 894.111/75. The recorded purport reports a possible understanding between the Japanese and German governments stipulating that the German government would not issue passports valid for travel to Japan to German Jews without prior entry permission from Japanese authorities.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers docket sheet recording correspondence regarding German Jewish immigration to Japan.
subfiles.summary: This document is a State Department List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.5562, subject 'Immigration to Japan from Germany'. It records a single communication (despatch/telegram No. 383) sent from Tokyo by Cameron on November 29, 1938, and cross-referenced to 894.111/75. The entry purports a potential bilateral arrangement between the Japanese and German governments requiring prior Japanese authorization before German passports valid for travel to Japan could be issued to German Jews.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Immigration to Japan from Germany
